text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

* An internal document of the office of the Secretary of State for Transport, made available to the paper, said the financial viability of TAP-Air Portugal could be at risk if a pilots' strike goes ahead this summer, which could force the state-owned airline to close. If TAP pilots go on strike from next Monday, as they have warned, the government may not be able to pay salaries to TAP workers in November.

* Lawyers of Portugal Telecom are studying ways to acquire capital of Brazilian telecommunications company Telebras since the Brazilian government cannot sell shares. The Brazilian government owns the minimum number of Telebras shares necessary to control the company.
* The report of the jury on the winning bid in the privatisation of chemicals company Quimigal will be delivered to Finance Minister Antonio de Sousa Franco next Monday.
* Galp joins price war among petrol stations.
* The Belmiro de Azevedo group is in talks to seek a foreign partner as part of its preparations to bid for a third mobile phone licence.
* Banks are preparing to offer cheap interest rates to football clubs that will be converted into companies from August 1.

* The profits of Portugalia Airlines will double this year. The company forecasts a net profit of 291 million escudos in 1997, a growth of 127 percent compared to 1996. The company registered a loss of 68 million escudos in the first semester of 1997.
